traces.scenario: Competing fan faults with uncertain RPM, airflow, and vibration signatures.
A less informative measurement may be preferable when it is substantially cheaper.
Equal information-gain-per-cost measurements must resolve ties deterministically.
A tripped independent protection signal blocks measurement selection and operation.
Unknown protection state cannot be treated as clear.
Required observation channels are missing and must not be imputed as normal.
Observation timestamps are stale and must be refreshed before fault ranking.
Sensor observations conflict and require reconciliation before ranking.
Measurement units are incompatible or unresolved.
Every available measurement requires a qualified person or is prohibited by the declared profile.
The only low-risk candidate is unavailable and must not be selected.
All eligible measurements have identical outcome distributions under every hypothesis.
Invalid prior mass must be rejected rather than renormalized silently.
A conditional likelihood row that does not sum to one is invalid.
Every candidate measurement must declare likelihoods for exactly the declared hypotheses.
Duplicate candidate measurement identities make the contract ambiguous.
Zero-cost measurement entries are rejected rather than dividing by zero.
An explicit unknown-fault hypothesis remains in the probability mass instead of being erased.
Protection is tripped even though other observations are stale; protection takes precedence.
An empty candidate set must return no safe selection rather than inventing a test.
High-information measurements that exceed the declared operator/risk profile remain ineligible.
